title: ClipForgeContracts
description: The complete ClipForge wire protocol. The PWA and the worker are two independent implementations of the types defined here; both are generated from this file, so neither can drift from it. See docs/adr/0005-single-source-contracts.md. Every timestamp is an ISO 8601 date-time string, NOT a Firestore Timestamp: the store adapters convert at the boundary, which keeps this document language-neutral and lets the unit tier compare documents as plain JSON with no emulator running.

JobStatus.title: JobStatus
JobStatus.description: Lifecycle of a job. Transitions are defined in docs/PLAN.md 3.3 and enforced by clipforge.scheduler.lease.

JobType.title: JobType
JobType.description: ECHO is a no-op job of three artificial stages used to exercise the scheduler without touching media. CLIP is the real pipeline. PUBLISH is a separate, single-stage job created after a human approves a clip — publishing cannot be a stage of CLIP because it happens on the far side of a human decision that may take days.

StageStatus.title: StageStatus
StageStatus.description: A stage that is DONE is never re-executed on retry. That is what makes a crash during ANALYZE cost seconds rather than the twenty minutes of DOWNLOAD and TRANSCRIBE that preceded it.

StageName.title: StageName
StageName.description: Ordered pipeline steps. ECHO_* belong to the ECHO job type only.

Lane.title: Lane
Lane.description: Which scheduler lane a stage runs in. The GPU lane is depth 1 because Whisper and the LLM cannot be co-resident in 6 GB of VRAM (docs/PLAN.md 2.1).

StageError.title: StageError
StageError.description: Structured failure detail. Captured rather than raised so a failed stage can be inspected from the PWA without reading worker logs.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable cause the PWA can map to a written explanation — see IngestErrorCode for the ingest stage's vocabulary. Null when a failure has no classified cause, in which case the UI falls back to `message`. Typed as a string rather than an enum so each stage can own its own vocabulary without every stage's codes leaking into every error.

retryable.description: False marks a failure that will never succeed on retry (bad input, a rights refusal), so the scheduler fails the job immediately instead of burning its remaining attempts.

Stage.title: Stage
Stage.description: One idempotent, checkpointed step of a job.

peakVramMb.description: Peak VRAM observed through NVML while this stage held the ModelBroker lease. Null for CPU stages.

checkpoint.description: Opaque, stage-owned resume state. The scheduler persists and returns it verbatim and never interprets it.

Job.title: Job
Job.description: One pipeline run over one source. Stored at jobs/{jobId}.

uid.description: Owning user. Every security rule keys off this field.

sourceId.description: Set by the DOWNLOAD stage once ingestion resolves the submission to a source. Null until then.

submission.description: What the user actually submitted: a YouTube URL or a local file path. Kept verbatim and separate from sourceId, because a job must be re-runnable from the original input even if its source document was garbage-collected.

clipId.description: The clip a PUBLISH job acts on. Null for every other job type. Security rules read this to check the clip's rights attestation before allowing the job to be created at all.

notBefore.description: The job is not claimable until this instant. Null means claimable immediately. This is how a publish-at time is honoured: scheduling lives in the one predicate every claim path already consults, rather than in a second scheduler that could disagree with the first.

stages.description: Ordered. Executed front to back; DONE stages are skipped on retry.

leaseExpiresAt.description: Set on claim, extended by heartbeat. A RUNNING job whose lease is in the past is reclaimable by the reaper.

error.description: The failure that terminated the job, copied from the failing stage.

JobEvent.title: JobEvent
JobEvent.description: Append-only transition log at jobs/{jobId}/events/{eventId}. Never mutated, which is what makes it trustworthy when debugging a job that failed hours ago.

seq.description: Order within a single transition. One transition can emit several events at the identical instant — a reap emits LEASE_EXPIRED and REQUEUED together — and ordering by timestamp alone would then fall back to document id, which is random. The log is ordered by (at, seq).

IngestErrorCode.title: IngestErrorCode
IngestErrorCode.description: Why an ingest failed, in terms a user can act on. Phase 3 requires each of these to map to a distinct user-facing message rather than a stack trace: 'this video is age-restricted' is actionable, 'DownloadError' is not. Only RATE_LIMITED and NETWORK are worth retrying.

SourceProvider.title: SourceProvider
SourceProvider.description: local exists so the whole pipeline can be exercised from a committed fixture with no network, which is what keeps the integration tier runnable in CI.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: One ingested long-form video at sources/{sourceId}. The media itself never leaves the worker (docs/PLAN.md decision D3).

externalId.description: YouTube video id, or null for a local file.

contentHash.description: Hash of the downloaded media. Transcripts are cached against this, so re-ingesting the same video costs no GPU time.

localPath.description: Worker-local absolute path. Advisory only for the PWA, which can never read it.

pinned.description: Exempt from workspace garbage collection. Sources are large and the disk is finite, so GC is not optional — pinning is the escape hatch for one you are still working with.

lastAccessedAt.description: Drives least-recently-used eviction. Touched whenever a stage reads the file, not when the document is read.

TranscriptWord.title: TranscriptWord
TranscriptWord.description: Word-level timing. Load-bearing for boundary snapping (D4) and caption generation, which is why faster-whisper is configured with word timestamps enabled.

Transcript.title: Transcript
Transcript.description: Stored at sources/{sourceId}/transcripts/{modelVersion}, keyed by model so re-transcribing with a better model does not destroy the old one.

SubScores.title: SubScores
SubScores.description: The rubric from docs/PLAN.md. The LLM returns these; Python computes the weighted total (decision D5), so the weighting can be changed and every historical candidate rescored without re-running inference.

Candidate.title: Candidate
Candidate.description: An LLM-proposed clip window at candidates/{candidateId}, after deterministic boundary snapping.

startSec.description: Snapped to a silence boundary and a sentence end, not the raw LLM value.

proposedStartSec.description: The model's raw suggestion, retained so snapping can be evaluated against it.

total.description: Computed in Python from subScores. Never supplied by the model.

RightsBasis.title: RightsBasis
RightsBasis.description: Why the operator believes they may publish this clip. Publishing is disabled by default and no clip can be published without one of these recorded, together with who attested it and when. A null `rights` block means no attestation exists — which is a different thing from a weak one, and the gate refuses it. See docs/PLAN.md Phase 8.

ClipLocation.title: ClipLocation
ClipLocation.description: Where the authoritative copy of a rendered clip lives. LOCAL is the free-tier default: Cloud Storage for Firebase requires the Blaze plan, so on Spark there is no bucket at all and clips stay on the worker. REMOTE means a copy exists that any browser can fetch. See docs/adr/0009-spark-tier-local-artefacts.md.

Clip.title: Clip
Clip.description: A rendered artefact at clips/{clipId}. The FILE itself never enters Firestore. On the free tier it stays on the worker and is reachable through the worker's local file server; when Blaze is available the same document also carries a playbackUrl. Both states are first-class here on purpose, so enabling Blaze populates a field rather than migrating a model.

localPath.description: Absolute path on the worker. Always set, even once a remote copy exists — the worker still needs it to publish (decision D7).

playbackUrl.description: A URL any browser can fetch. Null on the free tier. Populated by the Cloud Storage adapter, and equally by a tunnel — this field is 'a URL', not 'a Firebase thing'.

storagePath.description: Object path within the bucket, when one exists. Kept alongside playbackUrl because deletion and rules key off the path, not the URL.

ClipPreview.title: ClipPreview
ClipPreview.description: What a phone can actually see when the clip file is not reachable. Stored at clips/{clipId}/preview/poster as base64 — a subcollection document, so the review-queue query does not drag image bytes on every read. Sized to stay well inside Firestore's 1 MiB document limit; at ~40-60 KB the 1 GiB free tier holds roughly 20,000 of these.

posterBase64.description: A single representative frame, JPEG, base64-encoded without a data: prefix.

filmstripBase64.description: Four frames tiled into one JPEG, so a reviewer gets a sense of motion rather than a single still.

TranscriptRef.title: TranscriptRef
TranscriptRef.description: What Firestore keeps about a transcript, at sources/{sourceId}/transcripts/{modelVersion}. The word-level segments themselves live on the worker: a 60-minute word-level transcript approaches Firestore's 1 MiB document limit, and the PWA never needs one whole — Candidate.transcriptExcerpt carries the part a reviewer reads.

localPath.description: Worker-local path to the full Transcript document, as JSON.

vadPath.description: Worker-local path to the voice-activity map produced alongside the transcript: the speech spans, whose gaps are the silences. Phase 5 snaps clip boundaries to those gaps, so it is worth persisting rather than recomputing. Its contents are deliberately NOT modelled here — it never crosses to the PWA, and this document is the wire protocol.

PublicationState.title: PublicationState
PublicationState.description: Lifecycle of one attempt to publish one clip to one platform. PENDING is written BEFORE the upload begins, which is what makes a retry reconcile against the platform instead of double-posting.

PublishPlatform.title: PublishPlatform
PublishPlatform.description: Where a clip was published. TikTok and Instagram are out of scope until v0.3+ — both need app review with materially harder approval paths.

PublishPrivacy.title: PublishPrivacy
PublishPrivacy.description: Defaults to unlisted. Publishing something to the world by accident is not recoverable in the way an unlisted upload is.

Publication.title: Publication
Publication.description: One publish attempt, at clips/{clipId}/publications/{pubId}. Doubles as the audit log: it records who attested the rights basis and on what grounds, so 'who authorised this and why' is answerable for any published clip without reading worker logs.

externalId.description: The platform's id for the uploaded video. Null until the upload completes.

rights.description: Copied from the clip at publish time rather than referenced. The attestation that justified THIS upload must survive a later edit to the clip, or the audit trail records the wrong reason.

quotaUnits.description: What this attempt cost. A YouTube upload is 1,600 of a 10,000 daily allowance — about six a day — so the budget is tracked rather than discovered on the seventh failure.

publishAt.description: Scheduled publish time. The worker holds the clip until then.

WorkerCapabilities.title: WorkerCapabilities
WorkerCapabilities.description: Advertised so the PWA can explain why a job is not progressing, rather than leaving it silently queued.

GpuInfo.title: GpuInfo
GpuInfo.description: vramFreeMb is measured through NVML rather than tracked internally, because a foreign process (an interactive Ollama session, say) can hold VRAM the pipeline needs. Observed in Phase 0.

WorkerHeartbeat.title: WorkerHeartbeat
WorkerHeartbeat.description: Liveness and capability advertisement at workers/{workerId}.

LlmClipProposal.title: LlmClipProposal
LlmClipProposal.description: One window as the model returns it. Deliberately carries no total and no precise boundaries: the model supplies judgement, Python supplies arithmetic (D5) and boundary precision (D4).

LlmClipResponse.title: LlmClipResponse
LlmClipResponse.description: The schema-constrained response from the local model for one transcript window. Passed to Ollama as a format constraint so malformed output is rejected by the runtime rather than parsed defensively here.
